(D)uplicate (D)oses Barplot

Source: R/dd_barplot.R
dd_barplot.Rd

Generates a bar plot of duplicate (or repeated) records from the output of dd_rate, showing either their percentage or their number. The disaggregations are detected from data: geographic areas go on the x-axis if present, otherwise doses or birth cohorts, and dose or birth_cohort become panels when data also has geographic areas.

Usage

dd_barplot(
  data,
  value = "rate",
  duplication = "duplicate",
  within_ADM1 = NULL,
  min_total = NULL
)

Arguments

data

The output from the immunabc::dd_rate function.

value

Character. What to show on the y-axis: "rate" (default), the percentage of records in the duplication category, which shows where the problem is proportionally worst; or "n", their number, which shows where most records need correcting.

duplication

Character. Which records to show: "duplicate" (default), the extra records with the same person, dose, vaccination date and place of occurrence as an earlier record, which is the indicator; or "repeated", the extra records with the same person and dose but a different date or place.

within_ADM1

Character (optional). When analyzing data at the "ADM2" level, this optional character vector lets you specify one or several "ADM1" to filter. Default is NULL, which means no filtering by "ADM1".

min_total

Numeric (optional). Minimum number of records for a bar to be shown, since rates based on few records can be misleading. Hidden bars still count towards the dashed line. Default is NULL, which shows all bars.

Value

A ggplot object representing the bar plot.

Details

The y-axis is scaled to the data instead of 0 to 100, since duplicate records are usually a small percentage of all records. When showing rates, a dashed line shows the rate of all groups combined.
